platform: Omarchy 4.5.0-3, Hyprland 0.56.2, kernel 7.2.15-1-omarchy, x86_64, Quickshell 0.3.2, Node v26.13.0
scope: Live desktop acceptance of the 0.4.7 candidate: a clipboard read that did not finish normally no longer changes the Settings field. The read was inserted whatever its status, and lib/capped-run exits 1 without forwarding a byte when the paste is larger than the cap and forwards whatever a timed-out producer managed to send while exiting with the producer's status, so a failed read could carry an empty or partial string. Inserting that over the selected value cleared the field, and an empty country was then persisted. Only a normal exit may change the field now, so a rejected or truncated transfer leaves the value and the selection alone. The 0.4.6 behaviour it builds on was re-checked on the same tree: the Settings page's two free-text values are drawn from key events rather than Qt text inputs, the clipboard is read only on an explicit paste under a two-second timeout and a 4096-byte cap, the country field takes exactly two letters, and the clipboard picker pastes into the field.
install: The development symlink was unlinked (the repository untouched) and the plugin installed from https://github.com/salmun-nister/omarchy-loot-drops with `omarchy plugin add ... --enable --yes`, which cloned 53fbf68 (VERSION 0.4.7). The clone was checked out at v0.3.1 to stand in for the previous release, and the user's bar-slot entry was restored with both Epic mobile toggles, Amazon Luna, hideSeen and the country value, with epicNotify temporarily set false so the 0.3.1 baseline rewrite could not fire a burst during the update. The shell was restarted and `omarchy plugin update ... --yes` fast-forwarded the clone to 53fbf68; the bar-slot entry kept every value, including amazonEnabled, hideSeen, epicMobileAndroid, epicMobileIos, country and refreshMinutes. Each fetch rewrites seen.json ids, so the pre-lifecycle state file was restored from a backup after the lifecycle; install, update and removal themselves left it in place. Removal deleted the clone, unloaded the widget and removed its entries while seen.json stayed. The development symlink was re-linked, the plugins were rescanned, and the original shell.json and seen.json were restored byte-identically (sha256 166689b67848638039e9670674ab450783bb1a3ad3e8121e8f8bd5f6bb1bd395 and 3807bb74fea9a36ced0388d01019743d5b188767fbc5d8e79ace9565dbf34a1c) and the shell was restarted; the plugin loaded, the bar slot was back at its original index in the right section, and the three Epic ids were back in the baseline.
commands: restore the original shell.json and seen.json; omarchy restart shell

results.detail: ./tests/run passed 85 tests, the real Qt qmllint pass and the helper checks, both from the repository and from the installed clone. omarchy plugin validate . exited 0. validate_plugin.py reports valid with no errors or warnings and an advisory review-required security section with no findings. release_preflight.py reports READY, with advisory matches only. These are limited scans, not a security audit.

results.check: A failed clipboard read changes nothing
results.detail: The harness drives the real process callback with stand-in producers in place of wl-paste: one that sends more than the 4096-byte cap, so lib/capped-run exits 1 without forwarding a byte; one that sends a partial string and then hangs, so the helper forwards what was sent while exiting with the producer's status; and a control that finishes normally. The field held a selected value of DE for the first two and reported overflow=DE timeout=DE success=GB. The control proves the field was really driven, so a field that never had focus cannot pass. Reverting the field to the previous behaviour fails the same harness exactly as the finding describes: the overflow cleared the field and the timeout inserted the partial output. The unit tests drive the decision itself, including that the caret does not move when a paste failed.

results.check: Settings page with the self-drawn fields
results.detail: The live Settings page was captured on this desktop from the installed 0.4.7 clone and from the restored development symlink. Both show the country field at the same width as the dropdowns above it, with the two-letter hint, alongside the refresh interval and notification limit controls. The harness reports 14 settings rows and no QML errors, so the gear opens a populated page.

results.check: Typing, the country rule and the clipboard paste
results.detail: The owner drove the live panel on the tree that became 0.4.6, which 0.4.7 does not change in this respect: clicking the country field selects its value, letters are upper-cased and stop at two, a digit is ignored, Ctrl+V pastes, and SUPER+CTRL+V from the clipboard history pastes into the field, which previously did nothing. The agent cannot click the live panel, so the paste path was also exercised mechanically in a throwaway Quickshell scene (not part of the repository): a real EntryField behind a layer surface that takes the keyboard like the clipboard picker does, then the real /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-clipboard-paste-text --shift-insert. The field kept the focus item across the deactivation and the pasted value landed. The same scene with the previous behaviour, the field handing the keyboard back to a stand-in key catcher on any end of edit, left the field empty, so the check does detect the defect it guards.

The only clipboard read is the paste process: lib/capped-run as argv, with no shell, under timeout -k 1 2 and a 4096-byte cap that refuses an oversized read instead of truncating it, plus a four-second watchdog. Copying writes Quickshell.clipboardText and never reads. tests/qml-surface.test.mjs fails if runtime QML reintroduces a TextField, TextInput, TextEdit or TextArea, or reaches the clipboard outside that one path, and if the unconditional insert of a failed read comes back; it ran green in both the repository and the installed clone.

results.check: IPC actions on the live shell
results.detail: `markSeen amazon test-id-047` exited 0 and the id was written to the Amazon acknowledged set in seen.json. `openGame notastore x` and `openGame steam 'bad id'` both exited 0 without opening anything, confirming the validation path. seen.json was restored byte-identically after the test.

./tests/harness/run against the live stores reported 13 rows with headers for Epic and Amazon only (Steam and GOG were empty, so they correctly had no section), laid-out content, the paste regression above, and no QML errors. This is the transport and layout check, not a substitute for a desktop pass.

results.check: Fresh install, update from 0.3.1 and removal
results.detail: Installed from the repository URL at 53fbf68 and enabled, then checked out at v0.3.1 with the user's entry restored and `omarchy plugin update ... --yes` fast-forwarding to 53fbf68. The bar-slot entry kept amazonEnabled=true, hideSeen=true, both Epic mobile toggles, country and refreshMinutes=90. `omarchy plugin remove ... --yes` deleted the clone and unloaded the widget; seen.json was left in place. The development symlink, the original shell.json and the pre-lifecycle seen.json were restored and verified by checksum afterwards, including that the widget returned to its original position in the bar.

The Settings page capture supplied by the owner was cropped to the panel, 430x614, and staged outside the repository for the release notes. 0.4.7 changes no rendering, so the capture still shows the shipped page.

limitations: The agent cannot click the live panel, so the typing, the two-letter rule and both paste routes were driven by the owner on the tree that became 0.4.6, and the paste path was additionally exercised mechanically in a throwaway scene that is not part of the repository. The failed-transfer paths of 0.4.7 are covered by the harness, which drives the real process callback with stand-in producers; they were not reproduced by hand in the live panel. No bundled or single-game notification was observed live in this run; that path is unchanged and covered by the model tests. Live store contents vary, and GOG's success path remains fixture-only because no giveaway was live. A bar-slot entry pre-seeded with the Epic mobile keys before upgrading from 0.3.1 can announce the current mobile games once, because 0.3.1 never recorded those ids; no released version shipped those keys, so a normal upgrade has them off, and epicNotify was muted for the lifecycle here. The clipboard boundary is checked by a static test, the harness and a mechanical scene, not by an audit of a hostile clipboard client. No security audit is claimed; the validators are limited scans.
